sources.title: D. Tataru, Carleman estimates, unique continuation and applications (Northwestern University, 1998 monograph draft)
sources.locator: Chapter 3.6 'Elliptic equations: singular weights and strong unique continuation' (printed pp. 89-90 of the draft): Theorem 3.50 (support in |x| <= rho and away from 0 implies (tau+1)^2 ||x|^{-tau-1} u| <= rho^2 ||x|^{-tau} Delta u|), Remark 3.51, Corollary 3.6.1 with the gradient term, and Theorem 3.52 (strong unique continuation under |Delta u| <= c(|u|+|grad u|)); Chapter 4.2 inspected for the cutoff-and-absorb pattern

contents.name: Theorem 3.50 with Remark 3.51 and Corollary 3.6.1: singular-weight elliptic Carleman estimates for the Laplacian with weights |x|^{-tau} and an explicit constant in the weight parameter
contents.support: The source proves, by the self-adjoint/skew-adjoint decomposition of the conjugated operator, essentially the same family of estimates the pair needs: support in |x| <= rho and away from 0, weight |x|^{-tau}, right-hand side |x|^{-tau} Delta u, constant (tau+1)^2 or tau^2. The pair's lemma is the three-dimensional integer-weight form with the exact constant 2/s, proved by the Plancherel multiplier identity on the spherical-harmonic modes and extended by compact-annulus H2 density; the two proofs are independent and both apply in the stated class.

contents.name: Theorem 3.52: strong unique continuation for H2 solutions of |Delta u| <= c(|u| + |grad u|)
contents.support: The source's continuation theorem is for the differential inequality with bounded coefficient, not the equation Delta psi = V psi with V in L-infinity-loc; the pair's theorem covers the bounded-potential case and the cutoff-and-absorb step follows the same pattern (localize, treat the commutator as an L2 error, absorb the potential term for large parameter, let the parameter tend to infinity), with the global step closed by polygonal propagation.

contents.name: Chapter 4.2 (Schrodinger equation): Carleman estimates, cutoff localization, unique continuation; Chapter 4.6 Maxwell estimates
contents.reason: The pair uses only the elementary three-dimensional radial estimate and its cutoff consequences. The Schrodinger and Maxwell Carleman estimates, the boundary Carleman theory (Chapter 3.4) and the pseudodifferential calculus of Chapters 1-2 are not consumed by any item of this page or by its consumers in this run.

sources.title: B. Davey, Quantitative unique continuation for the Laplacian plus a potential (arXiv:1903.04021)
sources.locator: Section 1 and Theorem 1: quantitative unique continuation for Delta + V in dimensions n >= 3 with V in L^t, t > n/2; the case t = infinity, n = 3 is the bounded-potential case used here

contents.name: Theorem 1: quantitative unique continuation for Delta + V with V in L^t, t > n/2
contents.support: Independent corroboration of the statement in the bounded-potential case: for n = 3, t = infinity the hypothesis V in L^t is satisfied by any V in L-infinity-loc on a bounded region, and the conclusion controls vanishing on a ball by a weighted norm. The pair does not import the quantitative bound; it proves the qualitative vanishing-set statement from the radial Carleman lemma, and this source is recorded as the independent treatment of the same theorem, not as the proof used. The source is a preprint.

contents.name: Quantitative stability estimates and the dependence of constants on the potential and the frequency
contents.reason: No item of this page states a quantitative doubling, three-ball or stability estimate; the consumers (scalar and vector exterior Helmholtz uniqueness) use only the qualitative vanishing-set form.

sources.title: A. Moiola, Scattering of time-harmonic acoustic waves: Helmholtz equation, boundary integral equations and BEM (University of Pavia, 2022 lecture notes)
sources.locator: Section 4.4.1 (Dirichlet-to-Neumann map defined by T_l = k H_l^(1)'(kR)/H_l^(1)(kR)); Section 4.4.4 (Rellich's lemma, Theorem 4.22) and the uniqueness discussion for radiating solutions; Section 5.5 (Green's representation, Theorem 5.17). The notes treat the plane case n = 2 throughout and state that the construction is the same in 3D

contents.name: Section 4.4.1: Dirichlet-to-Neumann map with diagonal coefficients T_l = k H_l^(1)'(kR)/H_l^(1)(kR) and its role in the truncated exterior formulation
contents.support: The three-dimensional spherical DtN map with coefficients t_l = k h_l'(kR)/h_l(kR) and its real/imaginary sign properties are scaffolded on the earlier page em-expanded-analysis-prerequisites (batch 16) through lem-em-outgoing-spherical-hankel-dtn-bounds and lem-em-sphere-outgoing-dirichlet-to-neumann-map; this source is the independent plane-case treatment of the same construction and is recorded to confirm normalisation and modal structure.

contents.name: Section 4.4.4: Rellich's lemma (Theorem 4.22) and uniqueness of the radiating solution; Section 5.5: Green's representation in the exterior domain
contents.support: The source proves that a radiating Helmholtz solution with nonpositive boundary flux integral on a large circle must vanish; the pair's F3 route reaches the same conclusion for a smooth obstacle by combining the first Green identity on the truncated exterior with the strictly positive imaginary DtN pairing and the bounded-potential unique continuation with coefficient -k^2. The source is recorded as the independent treatment of the same uniqueness statement; the modal-window normalisation differs (plane case) and the 3D spherical coefficients are supplied by the recorded F1-F2 lemmas.

contents.name: Sections 5-6 (boundary integral equations, discretisation, numerical analysis) and Section 2 (acoustic modelling)
contents.reason: The page builds no boundary integral equation, no discretisation and no acoustic model; the recorded F4 argument uses a variational Hilbert-space formulation with Fredholm theory and consumes no boundary integral operator.

sources.title: B. Schweizer, Lecture notes: The Rellich Lemma on the Helmholtz equation (TU Dortmund, 16 March 2026)
sources.locator: Theorem 1.1 (uniqueness for (Delta + lambda)u = 0 in R^n \ B_R(0) with u = 0 on the inner sphere and integral over the sphere of |u|^2 tending to zero); Lemma 2.1 (Rellich lemma: a nontrivial solution satisfies integral over the shell B_rho \ B_R of |u|^2 >= c_R rho for all large rho) and its proof steps, which reduce to one spherical-harmonic mode

contents.name: Theorem 1.1 and Lemma 2.1: uniqueness for the exterior Helmholtz problem with a radiation condition, via the Rellich growth alternative
contents.support: Recorded as the second independent treatment of the exterior uniqueness mechanism: the note proves that a nontrivial solution cannot have decaying shell energies, and derives that a solution vanishing on the inner sphere with vanishing shell flux vanishes identically. The pair's F3 uses the modal DtN sign and the bounded-potential continuation instead of the shell-flux form, so the note corroborates the theorem family, the role of the radiation condition and the use of the spherical-harmonic decomposition without supplying the proof route used here.

contents.support: The source develops the potential-theoretic setting of the multipole theorem (the Newtonian integral of a compactly supported density) and the Green identities behind the sphere-trace computations of the companion example. The exact spherical-harmonic coefficient form, the uniform tail bound and the ball boundary series are carried by the recorded H1-H3 lemmas and the DLMF/Axler treatments, not by this source.

contents.name: Chapter 4.1-4.12: weak and variational formulation of the Dirichlet problem, existence, Fredholm alternative, spectral theory of a self-adjoint elliptic operator, interior and boundary regularity
contents.support: Independent textbook-level treatment of the conclusions of the pair's elliptic existence-and-regularity theorem: weak solvability with an exact trace, classical interior/boundary regularity for smooth data on smooth domains, and the compact-resolvent/spectral background used by the cavity completeness branch. The pair's recorded proof route (the coercive variational solver B2, the trace chain, and the difference-quotient bootstrapping of B7) is the one used; this source corroborates the statements and their hypotheses.

contents.name: Chapter 3.1-3.11: Sobolev spaces, weak derivatives, approximation of Sobolev functions and Sobolev functions on domains
contents.support: The compact-annulus density step of the Carleman lemma (smooth compactly supported approximation in H2 with support kept away from the origin) is standard Sobolev approximation theory as developed in this chapter; the pair states it as a consequence of the published density corollary and the smooth-factor Leibniz rule, and this source is recorded as the corroborating treatment.

contents.support: Book-level independent treatment of the harmonic-polynomial decomposition and the zonal kernel that the multipole expansion uses; the pair states the addition theorem for a real orthonormal basis and the uniform zonal kernel expansion via the recorded H1-H2 lemmas, and this source corroborates the same decomposition and kernel structure (with normalised surface measure, one normalisation conversion away from the pair's unnormalised d sigma of total mass 4 pi).

contents.support: Independent treatment of the ball boundary branch (c): the Poisson kernel (1-|x|^2)/|x-eta|^n, its expansion into zonal harmonics and the convergence to arbitrary boundary data. The pair states the L2 version with uniform derivative convergence on smaller balls from the recorded ball series lemma and the continuous-data Poisson form; this source corroborates the same boundary-value statement.

note: Harvest for the A page em-boundary-and-spectral-prerequisites. The two new mathematical suppliers thm-bounded-potential-weak-unique-continuation-in-three-dimensions and lem-three-dimensional-radial-carleman-integer-weight are authored locally from the recorded root research argument, with Tataru's monograph (Theorem 3.50, Corollary 3.6.1, Theorem 3.52) and Davey's quantitative continuation paper as independent treatments of the same estimates and theorem. The exterior multipole basis theorem composes the recorded H1-H3 lemmas with the Axler-Bourdon-Ramey book (harmonic polynomials, zonal kernels, Poisson kernel) and the DLMF entries; the Newtonian-potential setting is corroborated by Hunter's chapter 2. The exterior scalar and vector Helmholtz results compose the recorded F1-F2 DtN lemmas with the Rellich-type uniqueness treatments (Moiola, Schweizer). The elliptic existence-and-regularity theorem and the PEC spectral completeness compose the recorded B1-B7 and G1-G3 branches with Hunter's chapter 4 and Arbenz's formulation. Every declined source row carries its own reason; the reference-work and already-published rows record corroboration only, not new items. Seven of the eleven sources (Tataru, Davey, Moiola, Schweizer, Hunter, HFT, Arbenz) are not previously used by any batch of this run; Dyatlov and the three DLMF sections are shared with earlier batches as independent treatments of already-published suppliers.
